import html from typing import List # Predefined template for the post. The placeholders are used with str.format(). USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{post_heading}

Author: {user_name}

{post_content}
{post_tags}
""" def build_post_html( user_name: str, post_heading: str, post_content: str, post_tags: List[str] ) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- user_name : str The author's name. post_heading : str The title of the post. post_content : str The body content of the post. post_tags : list[str] A list of tags associated with the post. Returns ------- str The HTML string ready for display. """ # Validate input types if not isinstance(post_tags, list): raise TypeError("post_tags must be a list of strings") # Escape user supplied text to avoid XSS safe_user_name = html.escape(user_name, quote=True) safe_post_heading = html.escape(post_heading, quote=True) safe_post_content = html.escape(post_content) # Build the tags section tag_spans = [] for tag in post_tags: if not isinstance(tag, str): raise TypeError("Each tag must be a string") escaped_tag = html.escape(tag, quote=True) tag_spans.append(f'{escaped_tag}') tags_html = " ".join(tag_spans) # Format the final HTML html_output = USER_POST_FORMAT.format( user_name=safe_user_name, post_heading=safe_post_heading, post_content=safe_post_content, post_tags=tags_html ) return html_output.strip()
